fatal_errors: The hypothesis does not identify the relevant AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA or its as-cast FCC+B2 initial state.
It replaces intermediate-temperature aging at approximately 600°C and 750°C with unrelated high-pressure treatment, alloying, and generic microstructural engineering.
It does not specify or predict the approximately 550–750°C brittle window or the ductility minimum at 600°C followed by recovery at 750°C.
The proposed mechanism omits enhanced L12 ordering, increased antiphase-boundary energy, restricted cross-slip, planar slip, and crack initiation at jagged B2/FCC phase-boundary tips.
The cited studies concern strength–ductility optimization or deformation in other HEAs and do not demonstrate a thermally induced ductile–brittle–ductile transition.
The falsification experiment lacks a controlled aging-temperature series on a fixed alloy and cannot distinguish the target mechanism from generic microstructure–property changes.
explanation: The response recognizes compositionally complex alloys as the broad material class and suggests that phase structure can influence ductility, but it does not reconstruct the material, aging treatment, temperature window, structural mediators, or non-monotonic outcome. Its evidence supports only generic relationships between processing, phases, strength, and ductility in unrelated refractory or eutectic HEAs. None of the cited records establishes the claimed ductile–brittle–ductile behavior, and the suggested experiment would only test whether some unspecified alloy shows a transition rather than whether aging-induced L12 ordering and jagged FCC/B2 boundaries cause it.
